transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time: 10:15 AM PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Sofia Rivera (Redwood Product), Priya Shah (AuroraCloud - Head of Cloud Partnerships), Diego Ramirez (AuroraCloud - Platform PM), Lena Wu (AuroraCloud - Security Engineer)

[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey all, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off — I'm Jenna, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Marcus and Sofia with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya Shah: Morning, pretty good thanks, quick morning here in SF. Excited to walk through the integration requirements.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Hi folks, Marcus here, I'll lead the tech parts. Quick agenda: checklist for marketplace listing, reference arch requirements, packaging options, security Qs, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Diego Ramirez: Yep sounds good. We want to make sure we hit AuroraCloud marketplace's listing bar and also minimize on-boarding work for our operations team.
[00:40] Jenna Park: Great. Marcus, you want to kick off with listing checklist?
[00:44] Marcus Lee: Sure. So we've got a standard Redwood marketplace checklist — includes metadata (description, supported models, pricing tiers), screenshots, container/AMI/artifact, runtime requirements (GPU types, drivers), network reqs, and an integration test harness. We'll share the doc after this. Note: some of the wording in the doc references 'Dedicated' and 'Private' — might read odd in different marketplace contexts, so we'll tailor.
[01:10] Priya Shah: Can you send that doc please. Also, on pricing tiers — AuroraCloud would like options for marketplace customers to choose hosted (Redwood-hosted) vs BYO infra; is that something you support?
[01:23] Jenna Park: Yes, we support three modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). Marketplace listings typically prefer a BYO container/AMI flow plus a 'managed' listing where Redwood handles the hosted offering. We should capture both in the listing copy.
[01:40] Diego Ramirez: For BYO, we'll need image provenance and some attestation steps. We'd prefer an OCI image + deployment manifest, not an AMI unless necessary. Any constraints?
[01:52] Marcus Lee: OCI image + Helm chart is our recommended path for AuroraCloud. AMI is possible but more operational overhead. Important: for BYO, we need KV cache persistence explained and GPU drivers; also region/instance type matrix. We'll include a sample helm values file.
[02:15] Lena Wu: From security side, we need to understand data flow — does the container phone home? Where are logs stored? How do you handle customer keys?
[02:26] Marcus Lee: Good Q. For private deployments (VPC), no phone-home is required — optional control plane calls can be disabled. For hosted offerings we collect usage telemetry (token counts) and logs for billing; customers can opt out. For keys: we support customer-managed KMS via integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options for Private. Might be a bit fuzzy in some of our older docs — we'll provide exact doc links.
[02:55] Priya Shah: Could you drop links to SOC2 and encryption docs after? We have a compliance checklist we run on every partner.
[03:03] Sofia Rivera: Absolutely — we'll share SOC2, ISO attestation, and our KMS integration guide. Also I'll attach a short note on which modules require network egress (model download, telemetry) so you can list those in the marketplace description.
[03:20] Diego Ramirez: Great. Shifting to reference architecture — we need a diagram that shows cross-account roles, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, and how Redwood's control plane touches customer infra.
[03:33] Marcus Lee: For marketplace listing, we recommend a reference arch with two patterns: 1) BYO (customer runs Redwood runtime in their account): you'll deploy our container to a customer-managed cluster, we provide a CloudFormation/Helm template, cross-account IAM role is optional if you want managed upgrades; 2) Managed (Redwood runs in our infra): integration via VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink to keep traffic private. We'll outline both in the doc.
[04:05] Priya Shah: On PrivateLink vs peering — Aurora prefers PrivateLink for marketplace listings because it's easier for customers and doesn't require route modifications. Any blockers?
[04:16] Marcus Lee: PrivateLink is supported for our hosted offering; for BYO we'd normally use VPC endpoints for control plane comms. PrivateLink requires us to publish an endpoint service; we can support that. We'll note requirements for subnets and NACLs in the checklist.
[04:35] Diego Ramirez: Network performance — latency is a concern for inference. Do you have data on median p95 for different instance types? We need to show expected latency on the listing.
[04:47] Marcus Lee: We have benchmark profiles per model and instance type. For example, on A100-like hardware with 2048 context we see p50 ~80ms per token, p95 ~180ms — but it's model-dependent. We'll supply a performance matrix; some values might be approximate due to model variance. Also note quantized versions drop cost but can trade a bit on latency/quality.
[05:12] Priya Shah: Include a short note about model variants and quantization — important for customers comparing pricing.
[05:19] Sofia Rivera: Will do. We'll provide a short blurb for the marketplace that explains quantized vs FP16 vs INT8 tradeoffs and link to our Optimize toolkit suggestions.
[05:30] Diego Ramirez: About billing — how do you surface usage? Marketplace will want meter events or monthly invoice.
[05:37] Jenna Park: For managed hosted customers we can integrate with marketplace billing if you support it. For BYO we usually surface usage via logs/billing export and a reporting endpoint or invoice. We'll need to align on the marketplace's metering API; if Aurora supports metered billing for containers we can integrate.
[05:56] Priya Shah: We do have metering APIs for managed offerings. I'll add the docs link in the followup.
[06:02] Lena Wu: Security deep-dive — specific questions: do you support customer-managed keys for model encryption at rest? How are secrets rotated? Is there an audit log export to our SIEM?
[06:14] Marcus Lee: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; for RBAC we integrate with SAML/SSO and can issue role-scoped API tokens. Secrets rotation is supported via our secret rotation API that can be triggered by customers or automated schedule. Audit logs can be exported to CloudWatch/GCS/third-party SIEM via our logging hooks; we'll provide a sample pipeline.
[06:39] Priya Shah: Any known limitations for AuroraCloud customers in GovCloud or other isolated regions?
[06:45] Jenna Park: We have Private deployment options for air-gapped or isolated regions; those require an enterprise agreement and we normally do a design/engagement. For marketplace quick-listings, we typically call out supported regions in the metadata.
[06:58] Diego Ramirez: Packaging: you said OCI + Helm is preferred. We also want automated tests that run on our side before listing. What do you provide?
[07:09] Marcus Lee: We provide a lightweight test harness — a smoke test that runs desired endpoints (health, inference sample) and checks model response format. It's packaged as a GitHub Actions workflow and a test image you can run in CI. We'll provide the repo link. It checks model behavior, basic throughput, and auth flows.
[07:32] Priya Shah: Perfect. We'll run that as part of our pre-listing checks.
[07:36] Diego Ramirez: About image signing — we require signed images for the marketplace. Do you publish signed images?
[07:42] Marcus Lee: We can publish signed images and provide provenance via cosign signatures. For BYO customers they can verify signatures or build from source. We'll include instructions for cosign verification.
[07:54] Lena Wu: A few nitty-gritty items from security: minimum TLS versions, cipher suites, and support for mutual TLS for control plane connections?
[08:05] Marcus Lee: We require TLS1.2+ and strongly encourage 1.3. Mutual TLS is supported for private links/control plane — we can optionally require mTLS. We'll document supported ciphers and provide TLS config examples.
[08:22] Sofia Rivera: I'll capture those items in the security appendix of the checklist doc.
[08:27] Priya Shah: On joint go-to-market and listing assets — Aurora requires a screenshot of the UI, a short 50-100 word blurb, and a longer 300-400 word description. Any problem with us using the Redwood Console screenshots?
[08:40] Jenna Park: No problem, we'll provide high-res console screenshots and sample copy. We'll also include a short set of bullet points for benefits and an example pricing table.
[08:51] Diego Ramirez: A few timeline Qs — our marketplace release cadence is mid-April. If we want the listing live by 2026-04-20, what do we need?
[08:59] Marcus Lee: To hit 2026-04-20, ideally we finalize listing copy and assets by 2026-03-25, pass security/compliance checks by 2026-03-30, and complete any integration tests by 2026-04-10 to allow Aurora's QA. That's tight but doable.
[09:15] Priya Shah: Sounds doable. We'll aim for the 3/25 asset deadline.
[09:20] Lena Wu: On the compliance checklist you mentioned earlier, some of our internal auditors need a documented flow for PII and retention. Do you have a retention policy doc showing logs retention defaults and options?
[09:32] Marcus Lee: Yes, we have a retention policy doc with defaults (30 days for logs for hosted, configurable longer for customers) and export options. For private deployments the customer controls retention. We'll include that.
[09:44] Diego Ramirez: One more deployment question — autoscaling. If a marketplace customer selects Redwood-managed, do you support burst capacity? We need to show expected behavior for scaling to avoid SLA surprises.
[09:56] Marcus Lee: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst policies; for managed hosted we can offer burst capacity within plan limits or recommend a Reserved Dedicated plan for high predictable throughput. We'll include autoscale knobs and expected cooldowns in the doc.
[10:12] Jenna Park: Okay let's recap next steps — Marcus, Sofia and I will share the marketplace checklist, sample Helm chart, signed image details, SOC2/ISO docs, and a performance matrix. Priya and Diego will run the harness and share Aurora's metering API docs. Lena will pull compliance questions and send back specifics.
[10:31] Priya Shah: Yep, I'll add metering docs and schedule the reference arch follow-up for the week of 3/30.
[10:36] Diego Ramirez: I'll run initial tests once you share the sample image.
[10:40] Lena Wu: I'll compile the compliance Qs and share a list by 3/23.
[10:45] Jenna Park: Great. Any closing Qs?
[10:48] Priya Shah: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Marcus Lee: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links.
[10:53] Sofia Rivera: Thanks all.
[10:55] Meeting end.

Notes / links promised:
- Redwood marketplace checklist: https://redwood.ai/internal/marketplace-checklist (will share canonical link in follow-up)
- Sample Helm chart + values: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-samples

- Marcus Lee: Prepare AMI/container reference and sample Helm chart - due 2026-03-26
- Sofia Rivera: Draft marketplace listing copy + screenshots and send asset checklist - due 2026-03-25
- Marcus Lee / Jenna Park: Share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs - due 2026-03-24

End of transcript.
